audit_findings.title: The per-share outputs may mix Canadian-dollar cash flows with a U.S.-dollar market quote
audit_findings.mechanism: Currency translation affects comparison of CAD-denominated value_ps and buy_below with price_at_valuation, but does not alter underlying OE.
audit_findings.evidence: All dollar amounts set forth in this report are in Canadian dollars, except where otherwise indicated.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that the cash flows and valuation outputs are Canadian dollars, but the record does not identify the exchange or currency of the 129.70 quote. A USD quote compared directly with CAD intrinsic value would materially overstate relative value because CAD value per share must first be translated into USD. This is a possible dimensional error, not a demonstrated mismatch.
audit_findings.action: Identify the quote's exchange and currency, label all per-share outputs CAD, obtain the same-date CAD/USD rate, and rerun only the price, value and buy-below comparisons in one currency.

audit_findings.title: Perpetual growth may omit the full cost of replacing depleted reserves
audit_findings.mechanism: Insufficient reserve-replacement reinvestment would overstate forecast OE and the terminal value supporting 45.6%-50.9% of operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: To maintain production and cash flows over the long term, the company must replace produced reserves, which can be accomplished through exploration discovery of new resources, appraisal and investments in developing discovered resources, or acquisition of reserves.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that maintaining production requires discovery, appraisal, development or acquisitions, but it does not establish whether the OE maintenance-capex estimate includes their full-cycle cost. Because approximately half of operating value depends on a perpetual-growth terminal value, omission could change the valuation conclusion even though the omission itself is not yet demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile maintenance reinvestment to reserve replacement, appraisal, development infrastructure and acquisitions; then rerun the forecast and terminal value using the evidenced full-cycle requirement.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash settlements may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD468m scheduled for 2026-2027, equal to 11.5% of the CAD4,080.3m anchor; recorded ARO balance CAD3,530m
audit_findings.mechanism: ARO settlements are cash claims that must reduce forecast OE or be deducted separately in the equity bridge, without double counting amounts already captured in maintenance capex.
audit_findings.evidence: Estimated cash payments for asset retirement obligations are $ 241 million in 2026 and $ 227 million in 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes scheduled payments of CAD241m in 2026 and CAD227m in 2027. Their treatment in OE is unresolved. If omitted, the two-year cash claim is large relative to anchor OE and would overstate equity value; retaining accretion expense does not by itself capture settlement cash.
audit_findings.action: Trace historical and forecast ARO settlements through the OE calculation and maintenance capex, reconcile them to the CAD3.530b liability, and rerun with any uncovered settlements deducted once.

audit_findings.title: Some refinery and chemical closure obligations are not measurable or recorded
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecognized dismantling, disposal and remediation costs would reduce terminal OE or require a terminal equity-bridge reserve.
audit_findings.evidence: However, these sites generally have indeterminate lives based on plans for continued operations, and as such, the fair value of the conditional legal obligations cannot be measured, since it is impossible to estimate the future settlement dates of such obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms conditional legal obligations exist but says their amounts and settlement dates cannot be measured while the facilities have indeterminate lives. A perpetual DCF can omit these real claims, but the record cannot quantify their probability, timing or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Develop evidenced finite-life scenarios for each refinery and chemical facility and rerun with probability-weighted closure costs or a separately disclosed terminal reserve.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may violate the claim that all interest remains inside OE
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD105m in 2025, 2.6% of the CAD4,080.3m anchor; mechanically recurring at that amount would reduce base value by approximately CAD3.02 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest can disappear from equity-level OE if placed in excluded growth capex while its subsequent depreciation is added back.
audit_findings.evidence: Debt-related interest incurred in 2025, before capitalization of interest, was $131 million, compared with $192 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates CAD105m of capitalized interest, but not that it was excluded from OE. Its filed scale is 2.6% of anchor OE. Even treating the entire amount mechanically as a recurring omission would reduce base value from CAD123.30 to about CAD120.28 per share, leaving it below the CAD129.70 price and leaving the 30% margin-of-safety conclusion unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Trace the CAD105m through PP&E additions, maintenance-versus-growth capex and depreciation add-backs; correct the model if any portion is otherwise omitted.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor is contaminated by unusually large identified items
audit_findings.magnitude: CAD1,031m after tax, 25.3% of the CAD4,080.3m anchor; actual OE correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring classification of nonrecurring charges depresses anchor OE, while indiscriminate add-backs can overstate OE by ignoring subsequent restructuring and closure cash payments.
audit_findings.evidence: Current year results include identified items 1 of: $320 million after-tax ($421 million before-tax) related to the Norman Wells end of field life acceleration; a $306 million after-tax ($406 million before-tax) non-cash impairment charge of the Calgary Imperial Campus; a $249 million after-tax ($330 million before-tax) restructuring charge; and a one-time $156 million after-tax ($206 million before-tax) charge associated with the optimization of materials and supplies inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The identified items are material relative to the latest-year anchor. The record also shows mixed economic character: non-cash impairments, accrued restructuring costs, inventory effects and Norman Wells contractual obligations. Consequently, neither retaining all items nor adding all of them back is supportable without reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each item between net income, eligible D&A, asset write-downs, accrued liabilities and actual or forecast cash payments; then rerun the anchor and all scenarios using only item-specific adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to CAD1,141.8m in FY2020, 46.8% of filed D&A; adding all of it would move 2020 OE from negative CAD514.9m to positive CAD626.9m
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE and could affect trend diagnostics, but it does not enter the latest-actual 2025 anchor, shares or bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $1141.8m (46.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The unresolved classification can only understate FY2020 OE. Even the maximum computed adjustment affects a historical year that is not used numerically in the valuation because the anchor is 2025 latest actual rather than a trend. It therefore does not change the presented per-share values or buy-below threshold, although it could soften one reason for the too-hard flag.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2020 residual from filed depreciation schedules and rerun historical diagnostics only if evidence establishes an eligible non-economic add-back; retain the current valuation unless that evidence changes anchor selection.
